## Illustrative Example 2

```{r}

# ============================================================
# Bagging animation: regression trees appearing one-by-one
# ============================================================

# Packages
library(ggplot2)
library(rpart)
library(gganimate)
library(gifski)
library(transformr)

set.seed(4050)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. True function (your piecewise example)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
truth_fun <- function(x) {
  ifelse(
    x < 2,
    0.8*sin(2*x),
    -0.8 + 0.4*sin(5*x)
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Simulate data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
n <- 250
x <- runif(n, 0, 4.5)
y <- truth_fun(x) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.25)

df <- data.frame(x, y)

# prediction grid
grid <- data.frame(
  x = seq(min(df$x), max(df$x), length.out = 400)
)

truth_df <- data.frame(
  x = grid$x,
  y = truth_fun(grid$x)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Bootstrap regression trees
# ------------------------------------------------------------
B <- 100   # number of bootstrap models

pred_list <- vector("list", B)

for (b in 1:B) {

  boot_id <- sample(nrow(df), replace = TRUE)
  boot_data <- df[boot_id, ]

  fit <- rpart(
    y ~ x,
    data = boot_data,
    control = rpart.control(
      cp = 0.005,
      minsplit = 5,
      maxdepth = 30
    )
  )

  pred_list[[b]] <- predict(fit, newdata = grid)
}

pred_mat <- do.call(cbind, pred_list)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Dataset for individual bootstrap fits
# ------------------------------------------------------------
anim_df <- data.frame()

for (b in 1:B) {
  tmp <- data.frame(
    x = rep(grid$x, b),
    yhat = as.vector(pred_mat[, 1:b]),
    model = rep(1:b, each = nrow(grid)),
    frame = b
  )
  anim_df <- rbind(anim_df, tmp)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Running (bagged) average using cumulative means
# ------------------------------------------------------------
running_mean <- t(apply(pred_mat, 1, cumsum)) /
  matrix(1:B, nrow = nrow(pred_mat), ncol = B, byrow = TRUE)

avg_df <- data.frame(
  x = rep(grid$x, B),
  yhat = as.vector(running_mean),
  frame = rep(1:B, each = nrow(grid))
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Build animation
# ------------------------------------------------------------
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, colour = "grey50") +

  # true function
  geom_line(
    data = truth_df,
    aes(x, y),
    colour = "blue",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  # individual bootstrap trees
  geom_step(
    data = anim_df,
    aes(x, yhat, group = model),
    colour = "black",
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +

  # running bagged prediction
  geom_line(
    data = avg_df,
    aes(x, yhat),
    colour = "red",
    linewidth = 1.4
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Bagging Regression Trees",
    subtitle = "Bootstrap models used: {closest_state}",
    y = "Response"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +

  transition_states(frame, transition_length = 1, state_length = 1) +
  ease_aes("linear")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Render animation
# ------------------------------------------------------------
animate(
  p,
  fps = 10,
  width = 800,
  height = 500,
  renderer = gifski_renderer()
)
```

## Illustrative Example 3

```{r}

library(foreach)
library(doParallel)

set.seed(4050)

# Wages <- read.csv("Wages.csv")
# 
# 
# Wtrain <-  Wages %>% dplyr::sample_frac(0.80)
# Wtest  <- dplyr::anti_join(Wages, Wtrain,by="ID")




cl <- makeCluster(8) # use 8 workers
registerDoParallel(cl) # register the parallel backend

# Fit trees in parallel and compute predictions on the test set
predictions <- foreach(
  icount(160), 
  .packages = "rpart", 
  .combine = cbind
  ) %dopar% {
    # bootstrap copy of training data
    index <- sample(nrow(Wtrain), replace = TRUE)
    train_boot <- Wtrain[index, ]  
  
    # fit tree to bootstrap copy
    bagged_tree <- rpart(
      Salary ~ Job+Location+Province+FatherEducation+
        MotherEducation+GPA+Age+Experience+Education, 
      control = rpart.control(minsplit = 2, cp = 0),
      data = train_boot
      ) 
    
    predict(bagged_tree, newdata = Wtest)
}

predictions[1:5, 1:7]


predictions %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    observation = 1:n(),
    actual = Wtest$Salary) %>%
  tidyr::gather(tree, predicted, -c(observation, actual)) %>%
  group_by(observation) %>%
  mutate(tree = stringr::str_extract(tree, '\\d+') %>% as.numeric()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(observation, tree) %>%
  group_by(observation) %>%
  mutate(avg_prediction = cummean(predicted)) %>%
  group_by(tree) %>%
  summarize(RMSE = RMSE(avg_prediction, actual)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(tree, RMSE)) +
  geom_line() +
  xlab('Number of trees')


# Shutdown parallel cluster
stopCluster(cl)

```

## Illustrative Example 4

```{r}

set.seed(4050)


for (b in 1:6) {

  # bootstrap sample
  boot_id <- sample(nrow(Wages), replace = TRUE)
  boot_data <- Wages[boot_id, ]

  # fit tree
  tree_fit <- rpart(Salary~Job+Location+
                      Province+FatherEducation+
                      MotherEducation+GPA+Age+
                      Experience+Education,
    data = boot_data,
    control = rpart.control(cp = 0.01)
  )

  # plot tree
  rpart.plot(
    tree_fit,
    main = paste("Regression Tree", b),
    box.palette = "Blues",
    shadow.col = "gray",
    nn = TRUE
  )
}



```
